# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

**Implications for monitoring.** In the settings tested, what a model writes, it uses, in
proportion to the leverage of the written token, and what it does not write, it looks up
from a few prompt positions: the sources and copies stored at structural tokens next to
them. If this extends to other tasks, a monitor of internal state could focus on those
positions rather than the whole trajectory, and should track whether stored copies keep
growing with scale. The advice is weakest where the indirect path through generated text
is largest: 9 to 13% of persistence after filler, not yet split into late lookup and
relay, and one eighth to one fifth of the small stored hidden part in Qwen3-32B and the
Qwen3.5 hybrids.

**Why look up rather than relay?** Attention makes any earlier position readable at every
layer, so a later position can compute what it needs when it needs it. The stress tests
suggest that this is not the whole story. Even where three quarters of the layers can pass
a plan forward only through a recurrent state, the donor signal entering through the
attention layers accounts for nearly all of the effect, and at a distance the model relies
on a stored copy or loses the plan. Relay appears disfavoured when lookup is available,
not merely unneeded.

**What would overturn the principle.** Much longer generated text, reasoning with
thinking enabled, tasks that cannot be recomputed from the prompt, or training that
rewards concealment [@baker2025monitoring] could break it. Models trained to compute over
otherwise uninformative positions, with pause tokens [@goyal2024pause] or continuous
latent reasoning [@hao2024coconut], are designed to do what we rarely see, so the
principle is not an architectural law. Route accounting applies unchanged to each case.

## Limitations {#sec-limitations}

The generated spans are short, thinking is disabled, and the tasks are constructed; the
principle is established only for them. All-layer state edits are strong and can take a
model off its natural distribution, which the feature-steering replication and the
same-rhyme nulls address only in part. The hidden-choice controls do not distinguish a
stored pick from a stored copy of the list. The models span 1B to 32B parameters in three
families, with Gemma 4 31B for the hidden choice only. The accuracy collapse on unwritten
chains is correlational evidence for recomputation, not a causal test. Several committed
checks were not run: the Gemma 4 path split and induction control, the Qwen3.5
mixture-of-experts model, the Qwen3.5-27B recurrent test at 100 couplets (the decision
rests on 24), the Gemma 3 27B base model in the plain format, and the Qwen3-32B same-pick
null. Post hoc elements are labelled (Appendix @sec-app-prereg).
